papers.title: CFG
papers.full_title: Classifier-Free Diffusion Guidance
papers.sentence_en: Guides generation without a separate classifier by mixing conditional and unconditional predictions; now the default.
papers.research_why_en: Replaced the separately trained noisy-image classifier with one model trained both with and without its conditioning input, and combined the two score estimates at sampling time. It became the default guidance method in text-to-image systems.

evidence.note: Default '--scale 7.5' unconditional guidance; the sd-v1-3/v1-4 checkpoints use '10% dropping of the text-conditioning to improve classifier-free guidance sampling', linking arXiv 2207.12598.
'We apply progressive distillation to our video models with classifier-free guidance for fast, high quality sampling.'

evidence.source: Sander Dieleman, Guidance: a cheat code for diffusion models
evidence.note: 'A real game changer'; 'an essential component of OpenAI's DALL·E 2 and Google's Imagen'; GLIDE used it 'to great effect'.
Lecture 3-B is titled 'Classifier-free Guidance'.
7,480 citations, 1,079 influential.

papers.title: EDM
papers.full_title: Elucidating the Design Space of Diffusion-Based Generative Models
papers.sentence_en: Separated diffusion design choices (noise levels, preconditioning, loss weighting, sampler) into one framework; a default setup since.
papers.research_why_en: Recast diffusion models in one framework that separates the design choices: noise schedule and scaling, network preconditioning, loss weighting and sampler. With a second-order Heun sampler and retuned training it reached FID 1.79 on CIFAR-10 with 35 network evaluations. Its preconditioning, noise levels and samplers became the default setup that consistency models and many later methods build on.

evidence.note: One of 13 Outstanding Main Track Papers.

evidence.source: Sander Dieleman, The paradox of diffusion distillation
evidence.note: Calls Karras et al. 2022 an 'instant classic' and uses it as the reference study of sampler design.

Session 8 covers Elucidating Design Spaces (EDM), and session 9 is a DDPM and EDM code walk-through.

papers.title: Rectified Flow
papers.full_title: Flow Straight and Fast: Learning to Generate and Transfer Data with Rectified Flow
papers.sentence_en: Learns straight paths between noise and data, which makes few-step sampling easier; Stable Diffusion 3 and FLUX train with its formulation.
papers.research_why_en: Learned an ODE that moves along straight lines between noise and data, plus a 'reflow' procedure that straightens the paths further so one or a few Euler steps suffice. Stable Diffusion 3 and FLUX are trained with its linear-interpolation formulation.

evidence.note: 'Scaling Rectified Flow Transformers'; reports 'superior performance of this approach compared to established diffusion formulations'.
'FLUX.1 [dev] is a 12 billion parameter rectified flow transformer'.

evidence.source: Sander Dieleman, The paradox of diffusion distillation
evidence.note: Discusses reflow as a distinct path-straightening approach to fast sampling.
Lecture 12 is titled 'Rectified flow and flow matching'.
Entry #300, first under 'Distillation and Acceleration'.
4,391 citations, 449 influential.

papers.title: Flow Matching
papers.full_title: Flow Matching for Generative Modeling
papers.sentence_en: Trains generators by regressing the velocity of a chosen probability path, with diffusion paths as special cases.
papers.research_why_en: Trained continuous normalizing flows without simulation by regressing the velocity field of a chosen conditional probability path. Diffusion paths are special cases, and straight optimal-transport paths work better. Flow matching is now the training objective of large image, video and speech generators.

evidence.note: 'We use the Flow Matching training objective (Lipman et al., 2023) to train our generative model'; verified in the PDF text.

evidence.source: Flow Matching Guide and Code (Lipman et al., 2024)

Lecture 2 is titled 'Flow Matching'.
Entry #305.
Sessions 16-17 cover Flow Matching, and session 19 covers Conditional Flow Matching.
7,095 citations, 954 influential.

papers.title: Consistency
papers.full_title: Consistency Models
papers.sentence_en: Learns to map any point on a sampling trajectory straight to its endpoint, enabling one- or few-step generation.
papers.research_why_en: Trained a network to map any point on a probability-flow ODE trajectory directly to the trajectory's origin, enabling one- or few-step generation either by distilling a diffusion model or by training from scratch. It started a chain of one- and few-step methods, including LCM, CTM, sCM, shortcut models and MeanFlow.

evidence.source: Sander Dieleman, Learning the integral of a diffusion model (flow maps)
evidence.note: Says consistency models 'set off something of a chain reaction' of flow-map methods.
'Pioneering this direction, Consistency Models introduce a consistency constraint ...' (verified in the PDF text).

evidence.source: sCM: Simplifying, Stabilizing and Scaling Continuous-Time Consistency Models (Lu & Song, ICLR 2025 Oral)
evidence.note: Scales consistency models to 1.5B parameters; 1.88 FID on ImageNet 512x512 with two steps.
UIUC lecture 10 is titled 'Consistency models'; the Technion paper list includes Consistency Models as entry #301.
2,351 citations, 314 influential; the latent follow-up LCM adds 995.

edges.why: DDPM 'presents progress in diffusion probabilistic models [Sohl-Dickstein et al.]'. It keeps their forward and reverse latent-variable formulation and adds a new parameterization and a simplified objective.
edges.relation_zh: DDPM 沿用 Sohl-Dickstein 的扩散模型，生成出高质量图像。
edges.relation_en: DDPM took Sohl-Dickstein's diffusion models and made them generate high-quality images.
edges.relation_quote: We present high quality image synthesis results using diffusion probabilistic models, a class of latent variable models inspired by considerations from nonequilibrium thermodynamics.

edges.why: DDPM's simplified objective 'resembles denoising score matching over multiple noise scales' (citing NCSN). This is the paper's stated connection to denoising score matching with Langevin dynamics.
edges.relation_zh: DDPM 发现预测噪声的训练与 NCSN 的分数匹配等价。
edges.relation_en: DDPM showed its noise-prediction training is equivalent to NCSN's score matching.
edges.relation_quote: we show that a certain parameterization of diffusion models reveals an equivalence with denoising score matching over multiple noise levels during training and with annealed Langevin dynamics during sampling (Section 3.2) [55, 61].

edges.why: DDIM keeps DDPM's training procedure and replaces the Markovian reverse process with non-Markovian processes that 'lead to the same training objective' but sample faster.
edges.relation_zh: DDIM 沿用 DDPM 的训练方式，只换了采样过程，步数少得多。
edges.relation_en: DDIM kept DDPM's training as is and swapped in a sampler that needs far fewer steps.
edges.relation_quote: To accelerate sampling, we present denoising diffusion implicit models (DDIMs), a more efficient class of iterative implicit probabilistic models with the same training procedure as DDPMs.

edges.why: 'The methods of SMLD and DDPM can be amalgamated into our framework as discretizations of two separate SDEs.' DDPM becomes the variance-preserving SDE.
edges.relation_zh: Score SDE 把 DDPM 的逐步加噪写成连续时间的随机微分方程。
edges.relation_en: Score SDE rewrote DDPM's step-by-step noising as a continuous-time SDE.
edges.relation_quote: The methods of SMLD and DDPM can be amalgamated into our framework as discretizations of two separate SDEs.

edges.why: Classifier guidance follows 'Sohl-Dickstein et al. and Song et al. [Score SDE]' in conditioning with classifier gradients. It uses 'a score-based conditioning trick adapted from Song et al.' for DDIM sampling and adopts Score SDE's UNet changes.
edges.relation_zh: ADM 借鉴 Score SDE 用分类器梯度引导采样的思路，提出分类器引导。
edges.relation_en: ADM built classifier guidance on Score SDE's idea of steering samples with a classifier.
edges.relation_quote: Sohl-Dickstein et al. 2015 [56] and Song et al. 2020b [60] show one way to achieve this, wherein a pre-trained diffusion model can be conditioned using the gradients of a classifier.

edges.why: CFG starts from 'Dhariwal & Nichol (2021) proposed classifier guidance' and shows that the same fidelity-diversity trade-off can be obtained without the extra classifier.
edges.relation_zh: CFG 去掉 ADM 所需的额外分类器，改为混合有条件与无条件预测。
edges.relation_en: CFG removed ADM's extra classifier by mixing conditional and unconditional predictions.
edges.relation_quote: Dhariwal & Nichol 2021 proposed classifier guidance, a technique to boost the sample quality of a diffusion model using an extra trained classifier. ... We are interested in whether classifier guidance can be performed without a classifier.

edges.why: LDM trains the DDPM-style reweighted denoising objective ('the most successful models ... rely on a reweighted variant of the variational lower bound') in the latent space of a pretrained autoencoder.
edges.relation_zh: Latent Diffusion 把 DDPM 的去噪训练搬进自编码器潜空间。
edges.relation_en: Latent Diffusion ran DDPM's noise-prediction training on autoencoder latents, not pixels.
edges.relation_quote: The best synthesis quality is usually achieved when a reweighted objective [30] is used for training. ... we apply them in the latent space of powerful pretrained autoencoders.

edges.why: EDM starts from Song et al.'s SDE and probability flow ODE and re-expresses the VP and VE formulations in its common framework. Its experiments start from Score SDE's 'DDPM++ cont. (VP)' and 'NCSN++ cont. (VE)' models.
edges.relation_zh: EDM 从 Score SDE 的模型出发，重新调整噪声调度、采样器和训练。
edges.relation_en: EDM took Score SDE's models and retuned their noise schedule, sampler and training.
edges.relation_quote: “DDPM++ cont. (VP)” and “NCSN++ cont. (VE)” models by Song et al. [49] ... VP and VE benefit considerably from switching away from their original schedules. ... We start with the baseline training setup of Song et al. [49]

edges.why: FM notes that existing works use 'a connection between diffusion processes and continuous normalizing flows with the same probability path (... Song et al., 2020b ...)' and that its approach 'allows us to generalize beyond the class of probability paths modeled by simple diffusion'.
edges.relation_zh: Flow Matching 推广了 Score SDE 把噪声变成数据的路线。
edges.relation_en: Flow Matching generalized Score SDE's routes for turning noise into data.
edges.relation_quote: Flow Matching is compatible with a general family of Gaussian probability paths for transforming between noise and data samples—which subsumes existing diffusion paths as specific instances. ... We derive the vector field governing the Probability Flow ODE (equation 13 in Song et al. 2020b) for the VE and VP diffusion paths

edges.why: Rectified Flow positions itself against 'probability flow ODEs [Score SDE] and DDIM'. It shows them to be approximate special cases of its framework and uses straight paths to avoid their curved, expensive trajectories.
edges.relation_zh: Rectified Flow 不用 Score SDE 的弯曲路径，改走直线。
edges.relation_en: Rectified Flow replaced Score SDE's curved ODE paths with straight noise-to-data lines.
edges.relation_quote: In [73], three types of PF-ODEs are derived from three types of SDEs learned as score-based generative models ... the trajectories of VP ODE and sub-VP ODE are curved in general, and can not be straightened by the reflow procedure.

edges.why: Consistency models 'adopt the settings in Karras et al. (2022)' (noise schedule, T=80, time discretization, Heun solver). They 'use the same architectures ... as those used for EDMs' and slightly modify EDM's skip-connection parameterization.
edges.relation_zh: Consistency 沿用 EDM 的设定，把 EDM 蒸馏成一步生成器。
edges.relation_en: Consistency models adopted EDM's setup and distilled EDM models into one-step generators.
edges.relation_quote: We hereafter adopt the settings in Karras et al. 2022 ... In both consistency distillation and progressive distillation, we distill EDMs (Karras et al. 2022).

borderline.reason: Very strong case: 7,763 citations and 889 influential (Semantic Scholar, not re-fetched). It is covered in MIT 6.S184 lecture 4, Lilian Weng's 'Model Architecture' section and EleutherAI reading group session 27, and it is the backbone family behind SD3, FLUX and modern video models. Kept out because it changes the network architecture, not the diffusion or flow formulation, and the field scope does not list architectures. It belongs on an architecture roadmap and could be cross-listed here as a grey node.

6,017 citations and 463 influential (Semantic Scholar, not re-fetched). Introduced the cosine schedule and learned variances, which ADM builds on directly; covered in Weng's post and EleutherAI session 5. A refinement of DDPM rather than a new line.

Concurrent co-founder of flow matching; the Flow Matching paper names it with Rectified Flow as concurrent work, and the Movie Gen report cites it. Far less cited (1,148 citations, 50 influential, Semantic Scholar, not re-fetched). Flow Matching and Rectified Flow already represent this moment.

5,009 citations and 861 influential (Semantic Scholar, not re-fetched); the paper that established rectified flow at scale. Used here as adoption evidence for Rectified Flow. As a system paper it combines existing ideas rather than introducing one.

2,693 citations (Semantic Scholar, not re-fetched); entry #200 on the Technion paper list. A widely used training-free high-order ODE sampler. An important refinement of the DDIM and probability-flow sampling line rather than a line opener.

995 citations (Semantic Scholar, not re-fetched); brought consistency distillation to Stable Diffusion (LCM-LoRA). It is the main adoption route for consistency models, but a direct application of them.

928 citations and 133 influential (Semantic Scholar, not re-fetched). Shipped as SDXL Turbo and started an adversarial-distillation branch; Dieleman describes it as SDS combined with an adversarial loss. The main alternative to DMD as a distillation candidate; neither is on the roadmap.

ICLR 2025 Oral (re-fetched); scales consistency models to 1.5B parameters with 1.88 FID on ImageNet 512x512 in two steps, and its TrigFlow formulation unifies EDM and flow matching. Used here as adoption evidence for Consistency Models; a refinement of them.

ICLR 2025 (cited as such by MeanFlow), 458 citations (Semantic Scholar, not re-fetched). Conditions on step size for one-step generation. A MeanFlow predecessor in the flow-map family that MeanFlow's results surpass.

It is entry #304 on the Technion paper list, Dieleman's flow-maps post lists it among distributional distillation methods, and MeanFlow benchmarks against it. Same one-step-from-scratch family as MeanFlow with lower uptake (125 citations, not re-fetched).

Catalog member. Drops DMD's regression loss and adds a GAN loss with two-time-scale updates (772 citations, 138 influential, Semantic Scholar, not re-fetched). Widely used in practice, but a refinement of DMD.

Catalog member; ICLR 2025 Oral (re-fetched), 796 citations and 170 influential (Semantic Scholar, not re-fetched). Speeds up DiT training by aligning hidden features with pretrained self-supervised encoders. Influential, but a training-efficiency technique rather than a change to the diffusion or flow formulation.

borderline.short_title: JiT (Back to Basics: Let Denoising Generative Models Denoise)
borderline.reason: Catalog member; Li & He tech report (Nov 2025) arguing for clean-image (x) prediction with plain pixel-space Transformers. Too recent to show survey or adoption evidence; worth revisiting in 2027.

rejected_notable.reason: Highly cited text-to-image systems (Imagen is a NeurIPS 2022 Outstanding Paper). They integrate guidance, cascades and pixel or latent diffusion, and their method contributions are captured by the CFG and LDM nodes.

A conditioning adapter for pretrained text-to-image models (8,006 citations, Semantic Scholar, not re-fetched). It belongs to a controllable-generation or editing roadmap, not the modeling and sampling core.
Opened diffusion-based inverse-problem solving, the line DAPS belongs to (2,040 citations, Semantic Scholar, not re-fetched). An application subfield outside this roadmap's scope.

rejected_notable.short_title: Score matching (Hyvarinen 2005) and denoising score matching (Vincent 2011)
rejected_notable.reason: Mathematical precursors that predate deep diffusion generative modeling and have no arXiv versions. NCSN represents their entry into the field.

The distillation survey says it 'may be the first to distill pre-trained DMs', and Progressive Distillation calls it the closest prior work. It was superseded by progressive distillation, which the blogs, the reading group and Imagen Video feature.

Earlier (May 2023) one-step distillation via an integral KL divergence with an auxiliary diffusion model. Dieleman notes DMD 'arrives at a very similar formulation from a different angle'. DMD, a research core paper that is not on the roadmap, is preferred because DMD and DMD2 are the variants adopted downstream (CausVid, Self Forcing).
DMD says it 'draws upon inspiration and insights from VSD', so VSD is DMD's direct conceptual parent. Their target, test-time optimization of 3D representations, is outside this roadmap's scope.

Important for the SNR and continuous-time likelihood view, and covered in EleutherAI reading group session 7. No survey, blog or syllabus checked presents it as a turning point, and its practical design lessons are largely absorbed by Score SDE and EDM.

rejected_notable.short_title: Discrete diffusion (D3PM, MDLM, SEDD, Block Diffusion)
rejected_notable.reason: Diffusion over discrete tokens, mainly for language. It uses different math and has a different community, and deserves its own roadmap (MIT 6.S184 gives it a separate lecture).
Applies reflow to Stable Diffusion for one-step text-to-image generation; a direct application of Rectified Flow.

collection_members_not_on_roadmap.reason: A research core paper (Progressive Distillation) that is not on the roadmap; see the curation notes.
A research core paper (DMD) that is not on the roadmap; see the curation notes.

Refinement of DMD: it removes the regression loss, adds a GAN loss and two-time-scale updates, and scales to SDXL. Well cited and used in video distillation recipes, but DMD, a research core paper that is not on the roadmap, opened distribution-matching distillation. DMD2 makes a natural follow-up exercise.
A research core paper (MeanFlow) that is not on the roadmap; see the curation notes.

November 2025 Li & He tech report arguing that denoisers should predict clean images (x-prediction) with plain pixel-space Transformers. It draws expert attention but is too recent for survey or adoption evidence; borderline, worth revisiting in 2027.

ICLR 2025 Oral training-acceleration technique that aligns diffusion-transformer features with pretrained self-supervised encoders. Influential, but it changes training efficiency rather than the diffusion or flow formulation, and it also fits a representation-learning roadmap (it is on the Visual Generation roadmap).

ICLR 2025 Oral on discrete diffusion language models that interpolate with autoregressive decoding. Outside this roadmap's continuous diffusion and flow scope; belongs in a discrete-diffusion or diffusion-LM collection.

ICLR 2025 Spotlight on 4-bit post-training quantization of diffusion models. A systems and efficiency method that does not change how diffusion models are trained or sampled; fits a quantization or efficiency roadmap.
Inverse-problem solver based on decoupled noise annealing. Diffusion inverse problems are an application subfield, and within it DPS opened the line, not DAPS.

ICLR 2026 Oral on online RL fine-tuning of diffusion and flow models through the forward process. It is RL fine-tuning rather than a change to the diffusion or flow formulation; it is also a member of the RL collection.
April 2026 paper that post-trains generators with a Frechet-distance loss in representation space. Too new for evidence of field-level impact.

diffusion.curation_notes: Selection rule: high-confidence papers first, then papers that start or connect a line. Exactly 12 of the 15 researched papers were rated high. Progressive Distillation, DMD and MeanFlow (all medium) are not on the roadmap (listed above). Three arrows are not drawn because a longer path already connects the same papers: NCSN → Score SDE and DDPM → ADM (both via DDPM and Score SDE), and Score SDE → Consistency (via EDM). The start node is DDPM, centered on the canvas at column 1.5.

post-training.name: Post-training
post-training.scope: Turning a pretrained language model into an assistant: RLHF from human preferences to InstructGPT and DPO, AI feedback (Constitutional AI), instruction tuning (FLAN), parameter-efficient fine-tuning (Adapters, LoRA, QLoRA), and knowledge distillation up to on-policy distillation (GKD).

papers.title: Distillation
papers.full_title: Distilling the Knowledge in a Neural Network
papers.sentence_en: Introduced knowledge distillation: train a small student to match a large teacher's softened output distribution.
papers.research_why_en: Formalized knowledge distillation: train a small student to match a large teacher's temperature-softened output distribution. LLM distillation work, including GKD, MiniLLM and the Gemma 2 report, cites it as the base method.

evidence.source: Song & Zheng, A Survey of On-Policy Distillation for Large Language Models
evidence.note: Knowledge distillation was 'first formalized by Hinton et al. (2015)'. The survey treats it as the precursor of off-policy and on-policy LLM distillation.
'We also train the 2B and 9B models with knowledge distillation (Hinton et al., 2015) instead of next token prediction.'
Both open from Hinton-style KD. GKD uses 'Supervised KD (Hinton et al., 2015)' as a baseline, and MiniLLM starts from 'knowledge distillation (KD; HVD15)'.
About 26,891 citations, 2,967 influential.

papers.title: Christiano RLHF
papers.full_title: Deep Reinforcement Learning from Human Preferences
papers.sentence_en: Learned a reward model from human comparisons of two behaviors and used it instead of a hand-written reward for RL.
papers.research_why_en: Showed that a reward model fit to pairwise human comparisons of trajectory segments can replace a hand-written reward for deep RL on Atari and MuJoCo. RLHF pipelines for language models reuse this reward-model-from-comparisons template.

evidence.source: Lambert, RLHF Book, ch. Related Works
evidence.note: The chapter's reference for the start of modern RLHF: 'an application of RLHF applied to preferences between trajectories of agents within Atari games'.

evidence.source: Hugging Face blog 'Illustrating RLHF', Further reading
evidence.note: Listed among the early RLHF papers that come before the language-model work.
Tagged 'Landmark': 'The origin of RLHF: learning a reward from human comparisons. The recipe InstructGPT later scaled to language.'
'Our work can be thought of as an extension of RLHF [Christiano et al., 2017] with language models [Stiennon et al., 2020]'.
About 6,200 citations, 688 influential.

papers.title: Adapters
papers.full_title: Parameter-Efficient Transfer Learning for NLP
papers.sentence_en: Froze the pretrained model and trained small inserted bottleneck modules, starting parameter-efficient fine-tuning.
papers.research_why_en: Brought adapter-based parameter-efficient fine-tuning to pretrained transformers: freeze BERT and train small bottleneck modules inserted per task. It came within 0.4% of full fine-tuning on GLUE while adding 3.6% parameters per task. LoRA was designed to avoid the inference latency that adapter layers add.

evidence.note: Suggested reading, alongside LoRA.

evidence.source: Zhao et al., A Survey of Large Language Models, Sec. 5.3.1
evidence.note: Adapter tuning is one of the four representative PEFT methods it reviews (adapter, prefix, prompt tuning, LoRA).
'We focus on the original design by Houlsby et al. (2019)'. Uses it as the main adapter baseline and motivates LoRA by adapter inference latency.
About 7,578 citations, 919 influential.

papers.title: Ziegler RLHF
papers.full_title: Fine-Tuning Language Models from Human Preferences
papers.sentence_en: First applied a preference reward model plus PPO to a pretrained language model, with a KL penalty to the initial model.
papers.research_why_en: First paper to apply preference-based reward learning plus PPO to a pretrained language model, with a KL penalty toward the initial model. Stiennon et al. and InstructGPT follow this method, and DPO derives its loss from this KL-regularized objective.

evidence.source: Lambert, RLHF Book, ch. Related Works
evidence.note: 'Many canonical terms, such as learning reward models, KL distances, feedback diagrams, etc., were formalized in this paper.'

evidence.source: Princeton COS 597G (Fall 2022), 'Training LMs with human feedback'
evidence.note: Recommended reading, next to Stiennon et al.; InstructGPT is the required reading.
First entry under 'Key papers for LMs'.
DPO: 'We review the RLHF pipeline in Ziegler et al. (and later [Stiennon, Bai, Ouyang])'. InstructGPT: 'Our methodology follows that of Ziegler et al. (2019) and Stiennon et al. (2020)'.
About 2,790 citations, 213 influential.

papers.title: Stiennon RLHF
papers.full_title: Learning to summarize from human feedback
papers.sentence_en: Combined supervised fine-tuning, a reward model and PPO; people preferred its summaries to the human-written references.
papers.research_why_en: Adapted Ziegler et al.'s method to a supervised-fine-tuned starting policy and offline batches of human comparisons. With a reward model and KL-penalized PPO, its Reddit TL;DR summaries were preferred over the human reference summaries. This SFT, reward model, PPO sequence is the three-step recipe InstructGPT follows.

evidence.note: Slide 'More details and background from Stiennon'. The DPO derivation is presented as optimizing the implied reward 'via the Stiennon objective'. Ziegler 2019 does not appear in the slides.
Recommended reading for 'Training LMs with human feedback'.

evidence.source: Sebastian Raschka, 'LLM Training: RLHF and Its Alternatives'
evidence.note: Credits Stiennon et al. with introducing the 'popular RLHF three-step procedure' that InstructGPT later used. Also listed among 'Key papers for LMs' in the HF 'Illustrating RLHF' blog.

InstructGPT: 'Our methodology follows that of Ziegler et al. (2019) and Stiennon et al. (2020)'. Constitutional AI describes itself as 'an extension of RLHF [Christiano et al., 2017] with language models [Stiennon et al., 2020]'.
About 3,575 citations, more than Ziegler 2019.

papers.title: LoRA
papers.full_title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
papers.sentence_en: Trains low-rank updates to frozen weights that merge back for inference with no extra latency; now the default PEFT method.
papers.research_why_en: Trains low-rank updates to frozen weight matrices that can be merged back at inference with no extra latency. It became the default fine-tuning method in open-source tooling and the base of later PEFT variants such as QLoRA.

evidence.source: Stanford CS224N (2026) PEFT lecture; Princeton COS 597G
evidence.note: Suggested reading in CS224N; recommended reading in Princeton's PEFT lecture.

evidence.source: Hugging Face TRL docs, 'LoRA Without Regret' (not re-fetched)
evidence.note: Documents the Thinking Machines (2025) finding that LoRA can match full fine-tuning for SFT and RL when configured correctly.
'Parameter-efficient fine-tuning; why you can adapt huge models on one GPU.'
About 24,510 citations, 3,408 influential.

papers.title: FLAN
papers.full_title: Finetuned Language Models Are Zero-Shot Learners
papers.sentence_en: Introduced instruction tuning: fine-tuning on many tasks phrased as instructions lets a model solve unseen tasks zero-shot.
papers.research_why_en: Named and demonstrated instruction tuning: fine-tuning a 137B model on over 60 NLP datasets phrased as natural-language instructions improved zero-shot performance on held-out task types. It beat zero-shot 175B GPT-3 on 20 of 25 datasets. This made supervised instruction tuning a stage of its own.

evidence.source: Lambert, RLHF Book, ch. Instruction Tuning
evidence.note: Cited with T0 and Natural Instructions as the works that unified the task framework for instruction tuning.
Uses GPT-3 fine-tuned on FLAN (Wei et al., 2021) and T0 as the instruction-tuning baselines that RLHF is compared against.
Accepted as an oral at ICLR 2022.
About 5,523 citations, 488 influential; concurrent T0 has about 2,089.

papers.title: InstructGPT
papers.full_title: Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback
papers.sentence_en: Applied the SFT, reward model and PPO recipe to general instruction following; ChatGPT was trained the same way.
papers.research_why_en: Set the SFT, then reward model, then PPO recipe for general instruction following; outputs of a 1.3B InstructGPT were preferred over those of 175B GPT-3. OpenAI said ChatGPT was trained with the same methods, which made this the reference post-training pipeline.

evidence.source: Lambert, RLHF Book, ch. Related Works
evidence.note: Applied RLHF to instruction following. The ChatGPT announcement said it was trained with InstructGPT's methods, with some differences in data collection.

evidence.source: Sebastian Raschka, 'LLM Training: RLHF and Its Alternatives'; daily.dev reading list
evidence.note: Raschka: 'this training pipeline is based on OpenAI's InstructGPT paper' and is 'widely considered to be the approach behind ChatGPT'. daily.dev tags it 'Landmark'.

evidence.source: Stanford CS224N (2026) post-training lecture; Princeton COS 597G
evidence.note: CS224N lists OpenAI's 'Aligning language models to follow instructions'. It is the required reading of Princeton's human-feedback lecture.
About 25,112 citations, 2,509 influential.

papers.title: Constitutional AI
papers.full_title: Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback
papers.sentence_en: Replaced human harmlessness labels with AI feedback guided by a written set of principles (RLAIF).
papers.research_why_en: Replaced human harmlessness labels with AI preference labels guided by a written list of principles (RLAIF), and used model self-critique and revision to produce SFT data. The RLHF Book calls it the example that kickstarted RLAIF, now a default method in post-training.

evidence.source: Lambert, RLHF Book, ch. Constitutional AI and AI Feedback
evidence.note: 'the earliest documented, large-scale use of synthetic data for RLHF training'; 'kickstarted the broader field of RLAIF'; 'RLAIF has become a default method within the post-training and RLHF literatures'.

evidence.source: Raschka, 'RLHF and Its Alternatives'; daily.dev reading list
evidence.note: Raschka covers it first among the alternatives to RLHF. It is also on the daily.dev key papers list.
Includes a slide taken 'From Constitutional AI, Bai et al.' in the AI-feedback part of the alignment lecture.
About 3,866 citations, 264 influential.

papers.title: DPO
papers.full_title: Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model
papers.sentence_en: Turned the RLHF objective into a classification loss on preference pairs, with no reward model and no RL loop.
papers.research_why_en: Showed that the KL-constrained RLHF objective can be optimized directly with a classification loss on preference pairs, with no separate reward model and no RL loop. It became the default preference-tuning step in open models such as Zephyr, Tulu and Llama 3.

evidence.source: Lambert, RLHF Book, ch. Direct Alignment Algorithms
evidence.note: The most prominent direct alignment algorithm, which 'catalyzed an entire academic movement of aligning language models'. Lists its use in Zephyr-beta, Tulu 2/3, Llama 3 Instruct and Nemotron 4 340B.
'We also explored on-policy algorithms such as PPO, but found that DPO required less compute for large-scale models and performed better'.

evidence.source: Stanford CS224N (2026) post-training lecture; Stanford CS336 Lecture 15
evidence.note: Suggested reading in CS224N. CS336 gives DPO its own section ('DPO - RLHF without tears?').
One of two Outstanding Main Track Runner-Ups.
About 11,151 citations, 2,313 influential.

papers.title: QLoRA
papers.full_title: QLoRA: Efficient Finetuning of Quantized LLMs
papers.sentence_en: Trains LoRA adapters on a frozen 4-bit quantized model, so a 65B model fits on one 48GB GPU.
papers.research_why_en: Backpropagates through a frozen 4-bit (NF4) quantized model into LoRA adapters, which made fine-tuning a 65B model possible on a single 48GB GPU. It is built into bitsandbytes, PEFT and Transformers.

evidence.source: Hugging Face blog, 'Making LLMs even more accessible with bitsandbytes, 4-bit quantization and QLoRA' (not re-fetched)
evidence.note: Announced 4-bit loading and QLoRA training in the HF stack.
'4-bit fine-tuning of 65B models on a single GPU; democratized adaptation.'
Presented as an oral at NeurIPS 2023.
About 6,031 citations, 702 influential.

papers.title: GKD
papers.full_title: On-Policy Distillation of Language Models: Learning from Self-Generated Mistakes
papers.sentence_en: Trains the student on its own generated sequences with token-level teacher feedback, fixing the train-inference mismatch.
papers.research_why_en: Trained the student on its own sampled sequences with token-level teacher feedback under generalized divergences. This fixes the train-inference mismatch of supervised and sequence-level KD. With MiniLLM, it is one of the two papers that started on-policy distillation for LLMs.

evidence.source: Song & Zheng, A Survey of On-Policy Distillation for LLMs
evidence.note: GKD, 'alongside the concurrent MiniLLM (Gu et al., 2024), brought on-policy distillation into the LLM era in mid-2023'.
In Foundations and in the 'Start Here' path: 'Unifying formulation spanning on-/off-policy mixtures with flexible divergences.'

evidence.source: Gemma 2 technical report; Thinking Machines 'On-Policy Distillation' (Oct 2025)
evidence.note: Gemma 2: 'We also run distillation from the teacher on the student's distribution (Agarwal et al., 2024; Gu et al., 2024).' Thinking Machines: 'We extend prior on-policy distillation work by Agarwal et al' and Gu et al.
About 1,139 citations, 186 influential.

edges.why: Ziegler et al. carry Christiano's reward model from human comparisons over to language models ('Following Christiano et al. (2017), we ask human labelers to pick which of several values of y_i is the best response') and optimize it with PPO.
edges.relation_zh: Ziegler RLHF 把 Christiano RLHF 用到语言模型上。
edges.relation_en: Ziegler et al. took Christiano et al.'s preference reward model from simulators to text.
edges.relation_quote: this work has only recently been applied to modern deep learning, and even then has only been applied to relatively simple simulated environments (Christiano et al., 2017; Ibarz et al., 2018; Bahdanau et al., 2018)

edges.why: Stiennon et al.: 'Our approach is similar to the one outlined in [Ziegler et al.], adapted to the batch setting', adding an SFT-initialized policy and better human-data quality control.
edges.relation_zh: Stiennon RLHF 用更大模型和更好标注改进 Ziegler RLHF。
edges.relation_en: Stiennon et al. scaled up Ziegler's RLHF on summaries: bigger models, better human labels.
edges.relation_quote: Compared to [73], we use significantly larger models, move to the batch setting for collecting human feedback, ensure high labeler-researcher agreement, and make some algorithmic modifications

edges.why: InstructGPT: 'Our methodology follows that of Ziegler et al. (2019) and Stiennon et al. (2020)'. It takes their SFT, reward model and KL-penalized PPO steps from summarization to general instructions.
edges.relation_zh: InstructGPT 把 Stiennon RLHF 的三步法用于通用指令。
edges.relation_en: InstructGPT applied Stiennon's SFT, reward model and PPO steps to general instructions.
edges.relation_quote: Our methodology follows that of Ziegler et al. (2019) and Stiennon et al. (2020), who applied it in the stylistic continuation and summarization domains.

edges.why: DPO names InstructGPT among 'the standard approach [51, 40, 1, 28]' that fits a reward model and optimizes it with RL. It replaces the reward-model and PPO stages of that three-phase pipeline with one classification loss.
edges.relation_zh: DPO 用一个分类损失替代 InstructGPT 的奖励模型和 PPO 两步。
edges.relation_en: DPO swapped InstructGPT's reward model and PPO steps for one simple classification loss.
edges.relation_quote: We review the RLHF pipeline in Ziegler et al. (and later [40, 1, 28]). It usually includes three phases: 1) supervised fine-tuning (SFT); 2) preference sampling and reward learning and 3) RL optimization.

edges.why: LoRA is motivated by the inference latency of adapter layers ('We focus on the original design by Houlsby et al. (2019)') and uses them as its main PEFT baseline.
edges.relation_zh: LoRA 像 Adapters 一样冻结原模型，但增量能并回权重，推理不变慢。
edges.relation_en: LoRA froze the model like Adapters, but its updates merge into the weights: no slowdown.
edges.relation_quote: LoRA performs on-par or better than fine-tuning in model quality on RoBERTa, DeBERTa, GPT-2, and GPT-3, despite having fewer trainable parameters, a higher training throughput, and, unlike adapters, no additional inference latency.

edges.why: QLoRA backpropagates through a frozen 4-bit quantized model into 'Low-rank Adapters [28] (LoRA)', so LoRA is its trainable component.
edges.relation_zh: QLoRA 在冻结的 4 位量化模型上训练 LoRA，大幅降低微调显存。
edges.relation_en: QLoRA trained LoRA adapters on a frozen 4-bit model, shrinking fine-tuning memory.
edges.relation_quote: QLoRA backpropagates gradients through a frozen, 4-bit quantized pretrained language model into Low Rank Adapters (LoRA).

edges.why: GKD starts from 'knowledge distillation (Hinton et al., 2015)' and supervised and sequence-level KD baselines, and fixes their train-inference mismatch by training on student-generated sequences.
edges.relation_zh: GKD 沿用 Distillation 让学生学老师，但用学生自己写的文本。
edges.relation_en: GKD kept Distillation's student-learns-from-teacher idea, but on text the student wrote.
edges.relation_quote: One of the prevalent techniques for compressing models is knowledge distillation (Hinton et al., 2015). ... GKD trains the student on its self-generated sequences that are on-policy, instead of a fixed set of outputs sequences

borderline.short_title: HH-RLHF (Training a Helpful and Harmless Assistant)
borderline.reason: First paper to add to this roadmap. Required reading in Princeton COS 597G, in the HF 'Illustrating RLHF' key papers, and the RLHF Book says Anthropic used it extensively for early Claude. Constitutional AI trains its preference model 'following the process in [Bai et al., 2022]', and DPO evaluates on the Anthropic HH data. Left out because it is concurrent with InstructGPT and uses essentially the same recipe; Stiennon 2020 is the shared ancestor of InstructGPT and Constitutional AI (only Stiennon → InstructGPT is drawn).
CS224N 2026 and Princeton COS 597G both assign this paper rather than FLAN 2021, and Flan-T5 checkpoints were widely used (about 4,522 citations). It scales FLAN up rather than opening the line.
Concurrent with FLAN and required reading in Princeton's instruction-tuning lecture, but it has fewer citations (about 2,089 vs 5,523) and a smaller downstream footprint.

Origin of training students on teacher-generated sequences, which is what SFT-on-teacher-output distillation (Alpaca, DeepSeek-R1-Distill) does. GKD and MiniLLM both use it as a baseline. Left out to keep the distillation line at Hinton, then on-policy KD.

Concurrent with OPSD (ICML 2026 poster). According to an author's page it won a best-paper award at an ICLR 2026 workshop. It uses the feedback-conditioned model as a self-teacher for dense credit assignment and reports beating GRPO. It sits on the RL roadmap boundary and has fewer citations than OPSD per Semantic Scholar (332 vs 462; not re-fetched).

Concurrent self-distillation paper (ICML 2026 poster; ICLR 2026 workshop best paper per an author's page). The curated OPD list pairs it with OPSD as the 'no teacher at all' option. Popularized OPD as a cheap alternative to RL. OPSD cites it (Lu & Lab, 2025) more often than MiniLLM and takes its sampled-token reverse-KL variant from it. The curated list calls it the best single introduction. It is a blog post, not a paper, and its method extends GKD and MiniLLM.

Covered in CS336's DPO-variants slide and the most cited DPO variant checked (about 1,224 citations, NeurIPS 2024). The RLHF Book calls it 'a minor change to the DPO optimization' and says algorithm choice matters far less than data and the initial model.

Influential 'superficial alignment hypothesis' (1,000 curated SFT examples; S2: 1,513 citations, 138 influential, NeurIPS 2023). It is a data-quality analysis rather than a method later work builds on.

jepa-world-models.name: JEPA / World Models
jepa-world-models.scope: Prediction in representation space: the latent world-model roots (World Models, PlaNet), the non-contrastive methods JEPAs rely on (BYOL, VICReg), image and video JEPAs, and JEPA-style world models that plan in latent space (DINO-WM, PLDM, V-JEPA 2, LeWorldModel).

papers.title: World Models
papers.full_title: World Models (NeurIPS 2018 version: Recurrent World Models Facilitate Policy Evolution, arXiv 1809.01999)
papers.sentence_en: Learned a compact latent model of the environment from pixels and trained an agent inside its imagined rollouts.
papers.research_why_en: Learned a compact latent state from pixels (VAE + MDN-RNN) and trained a controller inside the model's own imagined rollouts. It revived the term 'world model' for deep learning and set the pattern of predicting a latent state forward in time.

evidence.source: Ding et al., Understanding World or Predicting Future? A Comprehensive Survey of World Models (ACM Computing Surveys)
evidence.note: States that Ha et al. 'significantly revived and popularized the term "world model" in 2018'.

evidence.source: Essentials of Embodied AI Research - World Models key papers
evidence.note: Listed first among 28 papers and marked essential.
2,238 citations (103 influential) for the arXiv record, plus 1,542 for the separately indexed NeurIPS version.
'World Models [26] pioneered learning policies directly from compact latent representations of high-dimensional observations.'
First entry (RWM, NeurIPS 2018) in its roadmap of world models in the deep learning era.

papers.title: PlaNet
papers.full_title: Learning Latent Dynamics for Planning from Pixels
papers.sentence_en: Planned actions purely in a latent space learned from pixels, using model-predictive control instead of a policy network.
papers.research_why_en: Introduced the recurrent state-space model and showed that an agent can choose actions purely by online planning in a latent space learned from pixels, using CEM-based model-predictive control with no policy network. DINO-WM, V-JEPA 2-AC and LeWM also plan with CEM over latent rollouts, though they drop PlaNet's pixel reconstruction.

evidence.source: Essentials of Embodied AI Research - World Models key papers
evidence.note: Marked essential.
2,270 citations, 268 influential.
Cites Hafner et al. 2019 for world models trained on raw sensory data and among prior planning work. DINO-WM itself plans with CEM inside MPC but does not attribute that planner to PlaNet.
Listed in the model-based RL lineage (PlaNet, ICML 2019), right after RWM.

papers.title: BYOL
papers.full_title: Bootstrap Your Own Latent: A New Approach to Self-Supervised Learning
papers.sentence_en: Avoided representation collapse without negative pairs, using a predictor and a slowly updated (EMA) target network.
papers.research_why_en: Showed that a joint-embedding method can avoid collapse without negative pairs, using an online predictor and an EMA target network with stop-gradient. I-JEPA and V-JEPA use this predictor/EMA-target asymmetry as their collapse-prevention strategy.

evidence.note: 9,252 citations, 1,355 influential.

Credits 'the non-contrastive collapse prevention strategy in BYOL (Grill et al., 2020)' as the strategy later made to work for image feature prediction, and cites BYOL for the EMA + stop-gradient + predictor setup it uses.
LeCun names BYOL first among the non-contrastive methods, followed by Barlow Twins, VICReg and I-JEPA.

evidence.source: Dawid & LeCun, Introduction to Latent Variable Energy-Based Models: A Path Towards Autonomous Machine Intelligence (lecture notes, 2023)
evidence.note: Lists BYOL, SimSiam and Barlow Twins as approaches to regularizing JEPAs and related architectures.

papers.title: VICReg
papers.full_title: VICReg: Variance-Invariance-Covariance Regularization for Self-Supervised Learning
papers.sentence_en: Made anti-collapse an explicit loss with variance, invariance and covariance terms, without EMA targets or negatives.
papers.research_why_en: Made anti-collapse an explicit objective with separate variance, invariance and covariance terms, with no EMA, stop-gradient or negatives. LeCun's own notes on the JEPA proposal use it as the example of how to train a JEPA, PLDM's world-model objective is VICReg-derived, and LeJEPA recovers it as a degenerate case of SIGReg.

evidence.note: 1,564 citations, 259 influential.

evidence.source: Dawid & LeCun lecture notes on the JEPA proposal (arXiv 2306.02572)
evidence.note: In the JEPA training section: 'let us give an example of how to maximize the information content of learned representations... The method is called variance-invariance-covariance regularization (VICReg)'.
'To prevent representation collapse, we use a VICReg-inspired objective, and inverse dynamics modeling.'
'LeJEPA recovers VICReg for this degenerate statistical test.'
Listed in the JEPA list's Theory, Analysis and Recipes section as the anti-collapse regularizer.
'Then, we came up with two other ones called VICReg and I-JEPA.'

papers.title: I-JEPA
papers.full_title: Self-Supervised Learning from Images with a Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture
papers.sentence_en: Predicts representations of masked image blocks from a visible context block, without pixel reconstruction or hand-made augmentations.
papers.research_why_en: Turned the JEPA proposal into a working, scalable image method. It predicts the representations of large masked target blocks from one context block of the same image, with an EMA target encoder and a predictor and without hand-crafted augmentations or pixel reconstruction.

evidence.note: 1,446 citations, 177 influential.
Milestone 2, the first concrete model in the list.
Built-in Transformers model with Meta checkpoints.
First entry under Core Architectures.

papers.title: V-JEPA
papers.full_title: Revisiting Feature Prediction for Learning Visual Representations from Video
papers.sentence_en: Extended JEPA to video: feature prediction alone learns representations of both motion and appearance.
papers.research_why_en: Extended JEPA from images to video. Feature prediction alone (no text, negatives, pretrained image encoder or reconstruction) produced frozen representations that handle both motion and appearance tasks, and the recipe became the base of V-JEPA 2.

evidence.note: 633 citations, 86 influential.

evidence.source: Ding et al., ACM Computing Surveys world-model survey
evidence.note: 'recent implementations such as V-JEPA and V-JEPA2 have demonstrated the practical viability of video-based self-supervised learning'.
Milestone 4: spatio-temporal masked feature prediction.
Listed in the self-supervised world model section.

papers.title: DINO-WM
papers.full_title: DINO-WM: World Models on Pre-trained Visual Features enable Zero-shot Planning
papers.sentence_en: Learned dynamics on frozen DINOv2 features from offline data and solved tasks zero-shot by planning in feature space.
papers.research_why_en: Showed that a latent dynamics model on frozen DINOv2 patch features, trained on offline trajectories without pixel reconstruction, rewards or expert demonstrations, can solve tasks zero-shot by CEM/MPC planning in feature space. It became a standard baseline for JEPA-style world models.

evidence.note: 505 citations, 86 influential.

evidence.source: Terver et al., What Drives Success in Physical Planning with Joint-Embedding Predictive World Models? (TMLR)
evidence.note: Abstract names DINO-WM and V-JEPA-2-AC as 'two established baselines'.

evidence.source: Hierarchical Planning with Latent World Models (Zhang et al., 2026)
evidence.note: Instantiates its planner on top of DINO-WM (Push-T), PLDM (mazes) and VJEPA2-AC (Franka).
Uses DINO-WM's PushT setup and dataset and its planning-solver configuration, and puts DINO-WM forward as the foundation-based family.
Listed among self-supervised world models alongside V-JEPA and V-JEPA 2.

papers.title: PLDM
papers.full_title: Learning from Reward-Free Offline Data: A Case for Planning with Latent Dynamics Models
papers.sentence_en: Trained a JEPA world model end to end from pixels on reward-free data with a VICReg-style loss, then planned with it.
papers.research_why_en: Trained a JEPA latent dynamics model end-to-end from pixels on reward-free offline data, preventing collapse with a VICReg-inspired multi-term objective plus inverse dynamics, and planned with MPC. Latent planning generalized to unseen layouts and to suboptimal data better than the offline RL baselines tested. LeWM later replaced this objective with SIGReg.

evidence.note: 'Among these baselines, PLDM is the closest to our setup, as it also learns a world model end-to-end directly from pixel observations.' LeWM's TwoRoom task is 'introduced by Sobal et al.', and LeWM counts its hyperparameter savings against 'the only existing end-to-end alternative'.

evidence.source: Delta-JEPA (Zhang et al., Jun 2026; independent group)
evidence.note: Uses PLDM, LeWM and Sub-JEPA as its Table 1 baselines.

evidence.source: Hierarchical Planning with Latent World Models (Meta, 2026)
evidence.note: Applies its hierarchical planner on top of PLDM for diverse-maze navigation.

evidence.source: No Gaussian Required: Contrastive Inverse Dynamics for JEPA World Models (Boylan & Hokamp, 2026)
evidence.note: Reports PLDM and DINO-WM as baselines: 'PLDM shows that a JEPA-style latent dynamics model can plan from reward-free offline data.'
118 citations, 23 influential; indexed as NeurIPS.

papers.title: V-JEPA 2
papers.full_title: V-JEPA 2: Self-Supervised Video Models Enable Understanding, Prediction and Planning
papers.sentence_en: Scaled video JEPA to a million hours of video, then added an action-conditioned predictor for zero-shot robot planning.
papers.research_why_en: Scaled V-JEPA pretraining to over a million hours of internet video, then post-trained an action-conditioned predictor (V-JEPA 2-AC) on under 62 hours of unlabeled robot video. The result was zero-shot pick-and-place on Franka arms in two labs by CEM planning in latent space.

evidence.note: 922 citations, 131 influential in about 16 months.
Open release of code, checkpoints and physical-reasoning benchmarks.

evidence.source: Terver et al., What Drives Success in Physical Planning with JEPA World Models? (TMLR)
evidence.note: Names V-JEPA-2-AC and DINO-WM as the two established baselines.
Milestone 9: world model for understanding, prediction and planning.

papers.title: LeJEPA
papers.full_title: LeJEPA: Provable and Scalable Self-Supervised Learning Without the Heuristics
papers.sentence_en: Argued isotropic Gaussian embeddings are optimal and enforced them with one regularizer, SIGReg, dropping training heuristics.
papers.research_why_en: Argued that isotropic Gaussian embeddings minimize downstream prediction risk and enforced them with one regularizer, SIGReg, which has a single trade-off hyperparameter. This dropped the stop-gradient, teacher-student and scheduler heuristics, and SIGReg was soon reused for JEPA world models (LeWM) and video pretraining.

evidence.note: 284 citations, 65 influential within 11 months.
'we adopt the Sketched-Isotropic-Gaussian Regularizer (SIGReg)' as its only anti-collapse term.

evidence.source: No Gaussian Required (Boylan & Hokamp, 2026; independent group)
evidence.note: Treats LeJEPA's SIGReg as the reference anti-collapse term and reproduces LeWM as its matched SIGReg control.

evidence.source: LeVJEPA (Kuhn et al., Aug 2026; shares authors with LeJEPA)
evidence.note: 'the first video encoder trained under LeJEPA's collapse-free objective'; reports matching or beating V-JEPA 2 at 5.6-20.8x less pretraining compute. Author-adjacent, not independent.

evidence.source: Turing Post LeJEPA explainer and 14 JEPA Milestones
evidence.note: Milestone 10, for simplifying training with SIGReg.

papers.title: LeWorldModel
papers.full_title: LeWorldModel: Stable End-to-End Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture from Pixels
papers.sentence_en: Applied SIGReg to an action-conditioned JEPA: a world model trained end to end from pixels with two loss terms.
papers.research_why_en: Applied SIGReg to an action-conditioned JEPA, giving a world model that trains end-to-end from raw pixels with two loss terms and one loss hyperparameter. Earlier approaches needed a frozen foundation encoder (DINO-WM) or a seven-term VICReg-derived loss with six tunable weights (PLDM). LeWM plans up to 48x faster than foundation-model-based world models.

evidence.note: 304 citations, 88 influential within 7 months.

evidence.source: Delta-JEPA (Zhang et al., Jun 2026; independent group)
evidence.note: Calls LeWM 'Our primary baseline and foundation'.
Direct extension that keeps LeWM's reconstruction-free JEPA setting and replaces step-by-step rollout with action-prefix prediction.

evidence.source: Independent reproduction of LeWorldModel on TwoRoom (Singh, Aug 2026)
evidence.note: Reproduces the result (94.0% vs about 87% reported) but finds that success swings from 84% to 8% with the goal-construction protocol.

visual-generation.name: Visual Generation
visual-generation.scope: Image generation outside the diffusion-sampling line: the VAE and GAN foundations, pixel-level autoregression, discrete visual tokenizers (VQ-VAE, VQGAN), text-to-image with tokens (DALL-E) and the CLIP embedding generators rely on, masked, scale-wise and continuous-token generation (MaskGIT, VAR, MAR), and representation alignment (REPA).

papers.title: VAE
papers.full_title: Auto-Encoding Variational Bayes
papers.sentence_en: Made latent-variable models trainable by backpropagation; later image tokenizers build on its encoder-decoder design.
papers.research_why_en: Introduced the reparameterized variational autoencoder, which made latent-variable image models trainable end to end by backpropagation. Later visual tokenizers build on its encoder-latent-decoder template: VQ-VAE, VQGAN, and the KL autoencoders used by latent diffusion and MAR.

evidence.source: ICLR 2024 Test of Time Award announcement
evidence.note: 'Auto-Encoding Variational Bayes' (Kingma & Welling) is listed as the Test of Time winner, selected from ICLR 2013/2014 papers.
17,261 citations, 3,106 influential.

evidence.source: MIT 6.S978 Deep Generative Models (Kaiming He), Fall 2024
evidence.note: Has a dedicated VAE lecture (09/12); CMU 10-423 also has a VAE lecture.

evidence.source: Bond-Taylor et al., Deep Generative Modelling: A Comparative Review of VAEs, GANs, Normalizing Flows, Energy-Based and Autoregressive Models (TPAMI)
evidence.note: VAEs are one of the five model families the review is organized around.

papers.title: GAN
papers.full_title: Generative Adversarial Nets
papers.sentence_en: Trained a generator against a discriminator; GANs led image synthesis until diffusion models took over.
papers.research_why_en: Introduced adversarial training of a one-step generator against a learned discriminator. GANs led high-fidelity image synthesis until diffusion models overtook them around 2021, and the adversarial loss is still a standard part of tokenizer training (VQGAN).

evidence.source: NeurIPS 2024 Test of Time Paper Awards
evidence.note: Test of Time award; called 'one of the foundational pieces for generative modeling', cited more than 85,000 times.

evidence.source: Chakraborty et al., Ten Years of Generative Adversarial Nets (GANs): A Survey of the State-of-the-Art (Machine Learning: Science and Technology, 2024)
evidence.note: A decade-long survey organized around the GAN framework introduced in 2014 and its variants.
'Generative Adversarial Nets' (Goodfellow et al., 2014) is the assigned reading for the GAN lecture; MIT 6.S978 also has a GAN lecture.

papers.title: PixelRNN
papers.full_title: Pixel Recurrent Neural Networks
papers.sentence_en: Generated images pixel by pixel with exact likelihood; a root of later visual autoregressive models.
papers.research_why_en: Framed image generation as exact-likelihood next-pixel prediction and introduced both PixelRNN and the convolutional PixelCNN. This autoregressive formulation is the root of later visual AR models, and VQ-VAE fitted a PixelCNN as the prior over its discrete codes.

evidence.source: Google Research blog, ICML 2016 research at Google
evidence.note: Marked as an ICML 2016 Best Paper Award recipient; the TWiML ICML 2016 recap (https://twimlai.com/articles/dueling-neural-networks-at-icml-plus-training-a-robotic-housekeeper-twiml-2016-06-24) lists it under Best Paper Awards too.

evidence.source: Autoregressive Models in Vision: A Survey (arXiv 2411.05902)
evidence.note: PixelRNN 'emerged as the pioneering work for AR image generation'; it anchors the survey's pixel-based category.
Required reading in the 09/24 Autoregressive Models session.
2,932 citations, 255 influential; the follow-up Gated PixelCNN paper has a further 2,846.

papers.title: VQ-VAE
papers.full_title: Neural Discrete Representation Learning
papers.sentence_en: Learned a discrete codebook of image tokens, then modeled the tokens: the tokenize-then-generate recipe.
papers.research_why_en: Learned a discrete codebook bottleneck (vector quantization with a straight-through gradient) and fitted an autoregressive prior over the codes. This set up the two-stage tokenize-then-model paradigm that VQGAN, DALL-E, MaskGIT and VAR all inherit.

evidence.source: Autoregressive Models in Vision: A Survey
evidence.note: 'A seminal work on discrete representation is VQVAE'; VQ-VAE, VQ-VAE-2 and VQGAN 'collectively established a two-stage paradigm for next-token prediction.'

evidence.source: A Comprehensive Survey of Discrete Tokenizers (arXiv 2502.12448)
evidence.note: VQ-VAE and VQ-GAN are described as 'the pioneers in image generation' among tokenizers.

evidence.source: Sander Dieleman, 'Generative modelling in latent space' (blog, 2025)
evidence.note: 'Autoregressive models of images took a huge leap forward with the seminal VQ-VAE paper.'
8,198 citations, 1,054 influential.

papers.title: StyleGAN
papers.full_title: A Style-Based Generator Architecture for Generative Adversarial Networks
papers.sentence_en: Redesigned the GAN generator with style modulation, producing photorealistic faces and an editable latent space.
papers.research_why_en: Redesigned the GAN generator around a mapping network, per-layer style modulation and noise injection. This produced photorealistic 1024px faces, a more disentangled latent space used for editing and inversion, and the FFHQ dataset. Later GAN work kept building on StyleGAN-family generators (StyleGAN2, StyleGAN-T, R3GAN).

evidence.note: 13,727 citations, 2,128 influential, more than BigGAN (6,329) or ProGAN (8,852); DCGAN is comparable (15,340 / 1,762).

evidence.source: R3GAN, 'The GAN is dead; long live the GAN! A Modern GAN Baseline' (NeurIPS 2024)
evidence.note: 'Using StyleGAN2 as an example, we present a roadmap of simplification and modernization'; it is an MIT 6.S978 required reading, together with StyleGAN-T.
The abstract names StyleGAN among the major GAN variants it summarizes.
Lineage chart VanillaGAN -> DCGAN -> PG-GAN -> StyleGAN -> StyleGAN2/StyleGAN3, with StyleGAN as the hub of later GAN architectures.

papers.title: VQGAN
papers.full_title: Taming Transformers for High-Resolution Image Synthesis
papers.sentence_en: Added adversarial and perceptual losses to VQ-VAE for sharp tokens modeled by a transformer; the default tokenizer.
papers.research_why_en: Added a patch-based adversarial loss and a perceptual loss to VQ-VAE and modeled the resulting codes with a transformer, producing compact, sharp discrete tokens. Its tokenizer became the default first stage for MaskGIT, VAR and LlamaGen, and the starting point for latent diffusion's autoencoder.

evidence.source: Autoregressive Models in Vision: A Survey
evidence.note: 'A significant milestone that unlocked the potential of autoregressive visual generation was the advent of VQ-GAN.'

evidence.source: Sander Dieleman, 'Generative modelling in latent space'
evidence.note: 'VQGAN became a core technology enabling the rapid progress in generative modelling of perceptual signals. Its impact cannot be overestimated.' Rombach et al. 'reused their previous VQGAN work' for latent diffusion.

LlamaGen: 'We use the same architecture as VQGAN'. MaskGIT: 'the same setup for the first stage as in the VQGAN model'. VAR: 'the same architecture as VQGAN but with a modified multi-scale quantization layer'.
The open text-guided generation method built on VQGAN ('using CLIP to guide VQGAN') that spread through the 2021 generative-art community.
4,718 citations, 707 influential.

papers.title: CLIP
papers.full_title: Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision
papers.sentence_en: Learned a shared image-text embedding that generators use for text conditioning, reranking and evaluation.
papers.research_why_en: Contrastive image-text pretraining produced a shared embedding that image generators use for text conditioning (Stable Diffusion's text encoder), sample reranking (DALL-E), guidance (VQGAN-CLIP) and evaluation (CLIP score).

evidence.note: 'uses a fixed, pretrained text encoder (CLIP ViT-L/14)'; 'Text prompts are encoded through a ViT-L/14 text-encoder.'
'we rerank the samples drawn from the transformer using a pretrained contrastive model (Radford et al. 2021).'
'Using CLIP to guide VQGAN' became the open text-to-image method of the 2021 generative-art community.
58,002 citations, 10,660 influential.

papers.title: DALL-E
papers.full_title: Zero-Shot Text-to-Image Generation
papers.sentence_en: Scaled the two-stage recipe to open-domain text-to-image with a 12B transformer over text and image tokens.
papers.research_why_en: Scaled the two-stage recipe to open-domain text-to-image generation: a discrete VAE tokenizer plus a 12B-parameter transformer that models text and image tokens as one sequence. Evaluated zero-shot, it was competitive with earlier domain-specific text-to-image models.

evidence.source: Autoregressive Models in Vision: A Survey
evidence.note: 'A pioneering effort in this field is exemplified by DALL·E' (text-to-image AR).
Listed as an optional recommended reading ('Zero-Shot Text-to-Image Generation (DALLE1)').
VAR: 'Trailblazing efforts like VQGAN and DALL-E'. LlamaGen (https://arxiv.org/html/2406.06525v1) lists VQVAE, VQGAN and DALL-E as the 'pioneering works' of AR image generation.
6,810 citations, 403 influential.

papers.title: MaskGIT
papers.full_title: MaskGIT: Masked Generative Image Transformer
papers.sentence_en: Predicts masked image tokens in parallel over a few refinement steps instead of one token at a time.
papers.research_why_en: Replaced raster-order decoding with a bidirectional transformer that predicts masked VQ tokens and decodes the whole image in parallel over a few refinement steps. It reports up to 48x faster decoding than autoregression in the CVPR version (64x in the arXiv abstract). Muse reused its masking schedule and decoding, and MAR recasts it as random-order autoregression.

evidence.source: eMIGM, Effective and Efficient Masked Image Generation Models (arXiv 2503.07197)
evidence.note: 'In image generation, MaskGIT (Chang et al., 2022) introduced masked image generation.'

evidence.source: Muse: Text-To-Image Generation via Masked Generative Transformers
evidence.note: Trains with a cosine masking rate 'as was done in (Chang et al. 2022)' and decodes with the same cosine schedule; Muse has 815 citations.
'masked generative models, e.g., MaskGIT and MAGE, can be generalized under the broad concept of autoregression.'
1,351 citations, 235 influential.

papers.title: VAR
papers.full_title: Visual Autoregressive Modeling: Scalable Image Generation via Next-Scale Prediction
papers.sentence_en: Generates images coarse to fine by next-scale prediction; a GPT-style model that beat diffusion transformers on ImageNet.
papers.research_why_en: Redefined image autoregression as coarse-to-fine next-scale prediction over a multi-scale VQ tokenizer. It reported that, 'for the first time', a GPT-style AR model surpassed diffusion transformers on ImageNet 256 while sampling much faster.

evidence.note: Main-track best paper.

evidence.source: Autoregressive Models in Vision: A Survey
evidence.note: 'A pioneering work that achieved this breakthrough is VAR'; it is the representative of the scale-based category.
Required reading.
1,230 citations, 198 influential in about 2.5 years.

evidence.source: NeurIPS 2025: 'Multi-scale Autoregressive Models are Laplacian, Discrete, and Latent Diffusion Models In Disguise'
evidence.note: A follow-up analysis paper that revisits VAR, showing it became a reference point.

papers.title: MAR
papers.full_title: Autoregressive Image Generation without Vector Quantization
papers.sentence_en: Showed autoregressive image models can generate continuous tokens with a small per-token diffusion head, no codebook.
papers.research_why_en: Showed that autoregressive image models do not need discrete tokens: a small per-token diffusion head (Diffusion Loss) lets AR and masked-AR transformers generate continuous latents. It also recasts MaskGIT-style masked generation as random-order autoregression.

evidence.note: Required reading.
774 citations, 147 influential.
'we utilize the Diffusion Loss (Li et al., 2024)' and 'strictly followed the open-sourced code of Li et al. (2024)'.

evidence.source: Autoregressive Models in Vision: A Survey
evidence.note: MAR 'provides a theoretical analysis suggesting that raster order and discrete representations are not necessary'.

papers.title: REPA
papers.full_title: Representation Alignment for Generation: Training Diffusion Transformers Is Easier Than You Think
papers.sentence_en: Aligns a diffusion transformer's hidden states with frozen pretrained features, speeding up training over 17x.
papers.research_why_en: Added a loss that aligns a diffusion transformer's hidden states with frozen pretrained encoder features (DINOv2 in its main results), which speeds up SiT training by over 17.5x. Follow-ups such as REPA-E extended the alignment to end-to-end VAE tuning, which made representation alignment a common design axis for generators.

evidence.note: Selected for an oral presentation (also stated in the arXiv comments).
Covered as a notable advance in training diffusion transformers.
Uses the REPA loss to make joint VAE and diffusion training work; 249 citations (Semantic Scholar).
796 citations, 170 influential in two years.

edges.relation_zh: DALL-E 用 CLIP 按图文匹配度给生成的图像打分，留下最好的。
edges.relation_en: DALL-E used CLIP to score its sampled images against the caption and keep the best.
edges.relation_quote: we rerank the samples drawn from the transformer using a pretrained contrastive model (Radford et al. 2021). Given a caption and a candidate image, the contrastive model assigns a score based on how well the image matches the caption.

edges.why: MaskGIT 'employ[s] the same setup for the first stage as in the VQGAN model' and replaces VQGAN's raster-order transformer with parallel masked decoding.
edges.relation_zh: MaskGIT 沿用 VQGAN 的分词器，改为并行填补被遮挡的词元。
edges.relation_en: MaskGIT kept VQGAN's tokenizer but filled in masked tokens in parallel, not one by one.
edges.relation_quote: Since our goal is to improve the second stage, we employ the same setup for the first stage as in the VQGAN model ... MaskGIT learns to predict randomly masked tokens by attending to tokens in all directions.

edges.why: VAR's tokenizer uses 'the same architecture as VQGAN but with a modified multi-scale quantization layer'.
edges.relation_zh: VAR 沿用 VQGAN 的分词器结构，改为多尺度量化，从粗到细生成图像。
edges.relation_en: VAR gave VQGAN's tokenizer multi-scale quantization to generate images coarse to fine.
edges.relation_quote: We employ the same architecture as VQGAN [30] but with a modified multi-scale quantization layer. ... redefines the autoregressive learning on images as coarse-to-fine “next-scale prediction”

edges.why: MAR argues that 'masked generative models, e.g., MaskGIT and MAGE, can be generalized under the broad concept of autoregression' and builds its masked-AR variant on that framing.
edges.relation_zh: MAR 沿用 MaskGIT 一次预测多个被遮挡词元的做法，但改用连续词元。
edges.relation_en: MAR kept MaskGIT's parallel masked prediction but used continuous tokens, not a codebook.
edges.relation_quote: Following MaskGIT [4], our MAR enjoys the flexibility of predicting multiple tokens at a time. ... This approach eliminates the need for discrete-valued tokenizers.

borderline.reason: Strongest candidate for promotion. A non-adversarial one-step generator trained by a drifting field computed in a self-supervised feature space (ImageNet 256: 1.54 FID at 1 NFE). The project page lists it as a NeurIPS 2026 Oral. It has 129 citations, 63 of them influential, after about 8 months (Semantic Scholar), and follow-ups already include DriftXpress (2605.12183), policy-learning variants (2605.07727, 2604.04528) and theory papers recasting it as score matching (2603.07514). It was widely discussed on X (e.g., https://x.com/iScienceLuvr/status/2019340015029919925). It is too recent to show downstream adoption, and its own related work places it near MMD moment matching. A re-check is due after NeurIPS 2026 and in 2027.

Set the convolutional GAN recipe (ICLR 2016). 15,340 citations, 1,762 influential; the 10-year GAN survey says it 'marks a significant breakthrough in the realm of generative AI, particularly for image generation', and the awesome-image-synthesis lineage graph puts it between the original GAN and PG-GAN/StyleGAN. Kept out only so the GAN branch has a single architecture node. StyleGAN builds directly on ProGAN, not DCGAN, so adding DCGAN cleanly would also need ProGAN.

28,275 citations, and its KL/VQ autoencoders are the most widely used visual tokenizers (MAR's KL-16 comes from the LDM codebase). Its main contribution, however, is diffusion in latent space, so it belongs on the Diffusion & Flow roadmap with a cross-roadmap edge from VQGAN.

The 'tokenizer is key' paper that introduced lookup-free quantization. It is an MIT 6.S978 required reading and has 727 citations; Dieleman notes that LFQ, FSQ and BSQ 'have gained traction'. It is the best candidate for a 'tokenizer refinements' node (which would anchor the rotation-trick exercise), but it refines VQGAN rather than opening a line.

841 citations. Open models showing that a plain Llama-style AR transformer over VQGAN-architecture tokens beats LDM and DiT, and a widely used baseline, but it introduces no new mechanism beyond VQGAN plus GPT.

Residual quantization; 1,009 citations. VAR calls its residual design 'akin to' RQ-Transformer, so it is a plausible direct precursor of VAR's multi-scale tokenizer. The survey evidence treats it as an improvement on VQ, not a turning point.
Replaces VQ with finite scalar quantization (ICLR 2024); 639 citations; an MIT 6.S978 optional reading. A simplification of the VQ step rather than a new paradigm.
Compresses an image to 32 one-dimensional tokens (NeurIPS 2024); an MIT 6.S978 required reading; 341 citations. It is too early to tell whether 1D tokenization becomes the default.

ICLR 2026 poster; 316 citations (61 influential) in a year. It replaces the VAE with a frozen pretrained encoder (DINO, SigLIP, MAE) plus a trained decoder, and explicitly avoids REPA-style 'auxiliary representation alignment losses'. It is the natural successor to DINOv2 and REPA if adoption continues.

Emu3 (821 citations; published in Nature in 2026) and Chameleon (1,015 citations) generate images by plain next-token prediction over VQ tokens inside one multimodal model, which extends this roadmap's token branch. PaperLeet has no multimodal collection, so whether this roadmap should carry one representative node is open.
Scaled AR text-to-image to 20B parameters (TMLR); 1,587 citations. It is closed and was quickly overtaken; DALL-E already represents the AR text-to-image step.
6,329 citations; the class-conditional ImageNet GAN baseline still reported in VAR and MaskGIT tables. StyleGAN represents the GAN-architecture branch instead.

The standard evaluation metric for every visual generator and the starting point of FD-Loss. It is a metric rather than a generation method, so it is better shown as a shared prerequisite. The Semantic Scholar arXiv record (517 citations) is split from the conference version, so the count is not comparable.

13,225 citations. MAR adopts 'the bidirectional attention implementation as done in MAE', and a latent-space MAE is Drifting Models' best feature encoder. Its primary home is a representation-learning roadmap.

rejected_notable.reason: A GAN training-stability refinement, superseded by later regularizers, with no lineage into current tokenizer or AR pipelines.
Direct precursor of StyleGAN (8,852 citations), folded into the StyleGAN node.
Refinements of StyleGAN (StyleGAN2: 7,295 citations), credited inside the StyleGAN node (R3GAN baseline).
Hierarchical refinement of VQ-VAE (2,518 citations); VQGAN is the refinement the field adopted as its default tokenizer.
Transformer-backbone refinement of VQGAN (847 citations); Muse chose VQGAN over it, and it did not become the default tokenizer.
Text-to-image scale-up of MaskGIT (815 citations) that reuses its masking schedule; counted as MaskGIT adoption evidence.
Scale-ups and variants of next-scale prediction (Infinity: 340 citations); they refine VAR.
GIVT (87 citations) was an earlier continuous-token AR model and MAGE (301) a masked generative encoder; MAR subsumed both lines and is the node the field cites.
Representation-alignment refinements (249 and 449 citations); credited to REPA and to DINOv2 (a research core paper that is not on the roadmap).
Pixel-level transformer autoregression, superseded by token-based AR. iGPT (an MIT 6.S978 optional reading) matters more for representation learning.
Diffusion backbones (DiT: 7,763 citations); DiT is assessed under Diffusion & Flow but is not on that roadmap, and both enter here only as the base models REPA regularizes.
Diffusion-based text-to-image systems, assessed (and not included) under Diffusion & Flow.

Hybrid unified multimodal models (MIT 6.S978 readings, 510-810 citations) that mix diffusion and AR inside an LLM; better placed on a multimodal roadmap. Emu3/Chameleon is the borderline representative.
Conditional image-to-image translation is a separate application line, despite pix2pix's 23,338 citations; the PatchGAN discriminator it contributed is credited inside the VQGAN node.
GAN text-to-image scale-ups that did not displace diffusion or AR; their MIT 6.S978 required-reading status is counted as evidence for the StyleGAN node.
Moment-matching precursors of Drifting Models with little adoption of their own.
A likelihood family that did not become an image-synthesis backbone; outside this roadmap's scope.
A 2021 community phenomenon rather than a method later work builds on; counted as evidence for the VQGAN and CLIP nodes.

collection_members_not_on_roadmap.reason: Contrastive self-supervised learning for recognition (26,740 citations), not a generation method. It is in this collection because Drifting Models computes its drifting field in a self-supervised feature space; the paper reports that public SimCLR and MoCo v2 encoders give 'decent results', but its latent-space MAE performs best. It fits as a prerequisite of the Drifting exercise or in a self-supervised representation collection (none exists besides JEPA / World Models).

Same situation as SimCLR. MoCo features appear only as alternative encoders: MoCo v2 in Drifting's ablations and MoCov3 in REPA's encoder comparison, where DINOv2 is the reference encoder. The generation field converged on DINOv2, so MoCo is a prerequisite at most, not a roadmap node.

ICLR 2025 oral that improves gradient flow through vector quantization compared with the straight-through estimator (68 citations, 6 influential). It refines VQ-VAE/VQGAN training, and there is no evidence yet that it became a default. It fits as an exercise hanging off the VQ-VAE/VQGAN nodes (it is also a member of the Retrieval collection).

Promising and heavily discussed: a NeurIPS 2026 Oral per its project page, with 129 citations (63 influential) and several follow-ups in about 8 months. It is still too new to show downstream adoption. It is the top borderline candidate, to be re-checked for promotion after NeurIPS 2026.

April 2026 objective that makes a Fréchet distance in representation space trainable (0.72 FID one-step on ImageNet 256). It has 42 citations (11 influential), no listed venue, and no adoption evidence yet. It is also a member of the Diffusion & Flow collection, next to the one-step distillation methods.

visual-generation.curation_notes: Selection rule: high-confidence papers first, then papers that start or connect a line. The research kept 13 papers. DINOv2, the only medium one, is left out, so REPA is shown without arrows. CLIP and DALL-E were announced together on 2021-01-05, and the DALL-E paper reranks samples with CLIP, so CLIP is placed first. SimCLR, MoCo, Rotation Trick, Drifting Models and FD-Loss stay in the collection list.
